test_cases.title: Default query params return 30d window, offset 0, limit 20 with full row shape
test_cases.given: a valid program_id with releases and no query params
test_cases.when: GET /api/overview/program-detail/{program_id}/releases is called by an authenticated session
test_cases.then: the endpoint defaults to range=30d, offset=0, limit=20 and returns rows shaped {ver, label, dot, tagColor, tagBg, date, stories, prs} plus relTotal
test_cases.objective: Verify the default query-param behavior and full response wire contract (FR-PGD03-1, FR-PGD03-2, FR-PGD03-4).
preconditions: Test DB seeded with a program having >=25 program_releases rows spanning >90 days
Valid bearer access token for any persona
steps: Send GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-001/releases with Authorization header, no query params
Inspect the JSON response body
expected_results: Response status is 200
At most 20 rows returned
Every row has exactly the keys ver, label, dot, tagColor, tagBg, date, stories, prs
stories and prs are string-typed
date is formatted like 'Jul 15' with no year
response includes relTotal reflecting the 30d window count
only rows within the last 30 days are present

test_cases.title: tagColor/tagBg hoisted to response top level, not per-row
test_cases.given: a program with multiple releases of different types
test_cases.when: the releases endpoint is called
test_cases.then: tagColor and tagBg are program-level fields on the response, not duplicated per row
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-PGD03-2's hoisting of tag_color/tag_bg to the top-level response object.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001 having releases of mixed types
steps: Send GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-001/releases
Parse the response body top-level keys and each row's keys
expected_results: Response top level contains tagColor and tagBg fields
Individual rows do NOT contain tagColor/tagBg keys
Values match the program's theme colours

test_cases.title: Range param filters rows to the requested window (7d/30d/90d)
test_cases.given: range=7d|30d|90d query params
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called for each range value
test_cases.then: only releases with date inside that window are returned
test_cases.objective: Verify range filtering excludes releases outside the requested window for all three supported ranges.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001 having releases at ages 2d, 10d, 45d, 120d
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=7d and record returned dates
Send GET .../releases?range=30d and record returned dates
Send GET .../releases?range=90d and record returned dates
expected_results: range=7d returns only the 2d-old release
range=30d returns the 2d and 10d releases
range=90d returns the 2d, 10d, and 45d releases (excludes 120d)
no release older than the requested window appears in any response

test_cases.title: offset/limit pagination returns correct page of rows
test_cases.given: offset and limit query params
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called with offset=20&limit=10
test_cases.then: the response returns the 10 rows starting after the first 20, ordered consistently
test_cases.objective: Verify offset/limit pagination slices the range-scoped result set correctly.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001 having 40 releases within 30d
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=30d&offset=0&limit=40 to capture the full ordered set
Send GET .../releases?range=30d&offset=20&limit=10
Compare the second response's rows to positions 20-29 of the full set
expected_results: Second response returns exactly 10 rows
Rows match positions 20-29 of the full ordered set
relTotal is unchanged between the two calls (same range window)

test_cases.title: limit above 50 is clamped to 50, not rejected
test_cases.given: limit=200 query param
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called
test_cases.then: the response returns at most 50 rows and status 200, not a validation error
test_cases.objective: Verify limit overflow is clamped to 50 rather than rejected (FR-PGD03-5, AC-2).
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001 having 80 releases within 30d
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=30d&limit=200
expected_results: Response status is 200
Number of rows returned is exactly 50, not 200 and not an error
relTotal still reflects the full 30d count (80), independent of the clamp

test_cases.title: limit exactly 50 is accepted unclamped
test_cases.given: limit=50 query param, the upper boundary
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called
test_cases.then: the response honors limit=50 exactly, confirming 50 is the inclusive boundary not the clamp trigger
test_cases.objective: Verify the boundary value 50 is passed through unmodified.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001 having 60 releases within 30d
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=30d&limit=50
expected_results: Response status is 200
Exactly 50 rows returned

test_cases.title: Invalid range value returns explicit 400, not FastAPI default 422
test_cases.given: an invalid range value (e.g. range=1y)
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called
test_cases.then: it returns 400 via an explicit validation check, never FastAPI's default 422
test_cases.objective: Verify range validation returns 400 explicitly per api-conventions, not FastAPI's auto-422.
preconditions: Any authenticated session, program_id may or may not exist
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=1y
expected_results: Response status is 400, not 422
Response body contains a JSON error message identifying the invalid range

test_cases.title: Cross-persona response is byte-identical for the same program and range
test_cases.given: authenticated sessions for two different personas (e.g. developer and cio)
test_cases.when: each calls the endpoint for the same program_id and range
test_cases.then: the request succeeds for both and the response bodies are byte-identical
test_cases.objective: Verify program_visibility is open-aggregate and the endpoint never persona-branches the response (FR-SH-13, A-004).
preconditions: Two valid access tokens for distinct personas (dev-bypass with role=developer and role=cio)
Program prog-001 exists with releases
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=30d with persona_a's bearer token
Send GET .../releases?range=30d with persona_b's bearer token
Byte-compare the two response bodies
expected_results: Both requests return 200
Response bodies are byte-identical (same rows, same order, same relTotal, same tagColor/tagBg)

test_cases.title: Any authenticated persona succeeds for any program_id (no per-program gating)
test_cases.given: an authenticated session not scoped to the target program via session.programs
test_cases.when: calling the endpoint for that program_id
test_cases.then: the request succeeds (200), confirming program_visibility does not gate by program membership
test_cases.objective: Verify the open-aggregate RBAC check passes regardless of session.programs scoping.
preconditions: Access token for a persona whose session.programs excludes prog-002
Program prog-002 exists
steps: Send GET .../releases with a token scoped to a different program
expected_results: Response status is 200
Release rows for prog-002 are returned

test_cases.title: Unauthenticated request returns 401
test_cases.given: no bearer token on the request
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called
test_cases.then: the response is 401
test_cases.objective: Verify unauthenticated callers are rejected with 401 per the AUTH-01 session baseline.
preconditions: No Authorization header set
steps: Send GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-001/releases with no Authorization header
expected_results: Response status is 401

test_cases.title: Unknown program_id returns 404 with JSON error body
test_cases.given: a program_id that does not exist
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called by an authenticated session
test_cases.then: it returns 404 with a JSON error body
test_cases.objective: Verify unknown-program handling matches the PGD-01 sibling endpoint's 404 convention.
preconditions: Valid bearer token
program_id 'nonexistent-999' absent from the database
steps: Send GET /api/overview/program-detail/nonexistent-999/releases with valid auth
expected_results: Response status is 404
Response body is JSON and contains an error message

test_cases.title: Release list scrolls without layout breakage when content exceeds visible area
test_cases.given: a program with 20 releases loaded into the panel (fills beyond the visible area)
test_cases.when: the ReleasesList panel renders on Program Detail
test_cases.then: the list scrolls within its fixed-height container without breaking the surrounding page layout
test_cases.objective: Verify the scroll container (max-height:296px; overflow:auto) contains overflow visually without layout breakage; no e2e framework is configured (test_e2e execution deferred per project-commands.yaml), so this is a manual visual check until Playwright is wired.
preconditions: apps/web dev server running against a seeded API with >=20 releases for a program
Program Detail page open in a desktop browser at /program/prog-001
steps: Navigate to /program/prog-001
Locate the Releases panel scroll container
Scroll within the container using mouse wheel / trackpad
Observe surrounding page layout while scrolling
expected_results: Container has max-height:296px and overflow:auto applied
Scrolling stays confined to the container; no reflow or overlap of adjacent panels
Page layout outside the container remains stable during scroll

test_cases.title: Independent range switcher on the panel does not affect PGD-02's chart switcher
test_cases.given: Program Detail page with both the token-trend chart (PGD-02) and the Releases panel (PGD-03) visible
test_cases.when: the user changes the Releases panel's own 7d/30d/90d switcher
test_cases.then: only the Releases panel refetches/re-renders; the PGD-02 chart's range selection is unaffected
test_cases.objective: Verify the two range switchers are wired independently, since no e2e framework is configured for automated verification.
preconditions: Program Detail page loaded with both panels populated, PGD-02 chart set to 7d
steps: Set the Releases panel switcher to 90d
Observe the Releases panel rows update to the 90d window
Observe the token-trend chart's selected range control
expected_results: Releases panel rows reflect the 90d window
Token-trend chart remains on 7d, unaffected by the Releases panel's switch

test_cases.title: Six-row loading placeholder shown while releases are fetching
test_cases.given: the Releases panel is fetching data
test_cases.when: the page renders before the API response resolves
test_cases.then: exactly six placeholder rows are shown (hint-placeholder-count=6)
test_cases.objective: Verify the loading state renders the mockup-specified six-row placeholder; no e2e framework configured so this is a manual check.

Navigate to /program/prog-001
Observe the Releases panel before data resolves
expected_results: Exactly six skeleton/placeholder rows render during loading
Placeholders are replaced by real rows once the API responds

test_cases.objective: Verify the closed status-indicator vocabulary mapping is applied correctly for all three kinds.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with one release of each of the three types for prog-001
steps: Send GET .../releases and inspect label/dot for each of the three seeded rows
expected_results: Feature release row has dot #1f8a5b
Patch release row has dot #2a6fdb
Hotfix row has dot #d1495b
label field matches the type name verbatim for each

test_cases.title: A release type outside the closed vocabulary raises a data-integrity error, not an unstyled row
test_cases.given: a program_releases row with type outside {Feature release, Patch release, Hotfix}
test_cases.when: the endpoint serializes the release list
test_cases.then: the service raises a data-integrity error rather than emitting an unstyled row
test_cases.objective: Verify out-of-vocabulary type values fail loudly instead of silently degrading the response.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with a program_releases row having type='Deprecated'
steps: Send GET .../releases for the program containing the invalid-type row
expected_results: Response is a 5xx server error (or documented error response), not a 200 with an unstyled/blank row
Error is logged/raised identifying the data-integrity violation

test_cases.title: relTotal uses the same date window as the returned rows for each range value
test_cases.given: a program with releases spanning well beyond 90 days
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called with range=7d, then range=30d, then range=90d
test_cases.then: relTotal for each call equals the count of releases actually within that same window, matching the row-level date filter exactly
test_cases.objective: Verify relTotal and the row query share an identical date-window predicate (catches an unbounded-count bug) across all three range values.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001: 3 releases at 2d old, 5 at 20d old, 10 at 60d old, 20 at 150d old
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=7d&limit=50 and record relTotal and row count
Send GET .../releases?range=30d&limit=50 and record relTotal and row count
Send GET .../releases?range=90d&limit=50 and record relTotal and row count
Independently compute expected counts per window from seed data
expected_results: range=7d: relTotal == 3, matching the 3 rows within 7 days
range=30d: relTotal == 8 (3+5), matching rows within 30 days
range=90d: relTotal == 18 (3+5+10), matching rows within 90 days; the 150d-old releases are excluded from both relTotal and rows
in every case relTotal equals the full in-window count even when limit truncates the returned rows

test_cases.title: relTotal reflects full window count even when limit truncates rows
test_cases.given: more releases in the window than the page limit
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called with limit smaller than the in-window count
test_cases.then: relTotal still reports the full in-window count, not the truncated page size
test_cases.objective: Verify relTotal is independent of pagination limit/offset, isolating the window-parity guardrail from the pagination slice.
preconditions: Test DB seeded with program prog-001 having 35 releases within 30d
steps: Send GET .../releases?range=30d&limit=10&offset=0
expected_results: Response returns exactly 10 rows
relTotal equals 35, not 10

test_cases.when: a range change or filter refresh request is issued
test_cases.then: the endpoint responds within the 2s budget (NFR-002), contingent on the program_releases(program_id, date) index (FR-PGD03-7)

preconditions: Test DB seeded with >=5000 program_releases rows for a single program_id
program_releases(program_id, date) index confirmed present (BED-01 migration)
steps: Issue 50 sequential/concurrent GET requests to .../releases?range=90d against the seeded program
Record response latencies
Compute p95 latency

EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the underlying query shows index usage on program_releases(program_id, date), not a sequential scan

test_cases.title: program_visibility RBAC check applied server-side with no dedicated audit event
test_cases.given: an authenticated request to the releases endpoint
test_cases.when: the request is processed
test_cases.then: program_visibility is invoked server-side (never UI-only hiding) and, being open-aggregate, emits no dedicated audit log event
test_cases.objective: Verify RBAC enforcement happens server-side and observability matches the open-aggregate design (no org_access/individual_view_denied/member_view_denied event emitted for this check).
preconditions: Structured logging capture enabled for the test run
Valid bearer token for any persona
steps: Send GET .../releases with a valid token
Capture structured logs emitted during the request
Attempt the same request with no token to confirm server-side (not client-only) enforcement
expected_results: Authenticated request succeeds (200) regardless of persona/program membership
No org_access/individual_view_denied/member_view_denied log event is emitted for this endpoint's program_visibility check
Unauthenticated request is rejected server-side (401), proving enforcement is not UI-only

test_cases.when: the request completes

steps: Send GET .../releases?range=30d&offset=0&limit=20 with valid auth
Capture the structured log entry for this request
expected_results: Log entry contains method=GET

Log entry contains program_id, range, offset, limit
Log entry contains status and latency fields
